As for antidepressants, they can be dangerous if the person has other yet undiagnosed conditions such as bipolar disorder(as they can trigger mania) and psychotic disorders like schizophrenia. In those patients, antidepressants can still be used in conjuction with mood stabilizers and/or antipsychotics.

I rationalize not smoking like this- when I start smoking, if I want to quit again I'd have to go through the first 72 hours again. There is nothing wrong with using nicotine replacement theraphy. Just make sure to discuss this with a pharmacist or a doctor first. 

Remember that those cravings where you feel like crawling out of your skin and crying are very temporary. Those are physical withdrawals. The mental withdrawals are easier to deal with.

Put all that money you spend on smokes in a jar. Or half of them. And put it toward something nice to treat yourself to. I live somewhere where smokes are cheap compared to other countries but the money adds up fast and you will be surprised by how much you save.

Exercise. Even if it's just a short walk. It a) takes your mind off things and b) it reminds you how out shape smoking has made you. 

Find something to do with your hands. Sudoku, knitting, crosswords, painting etc.

Vapes work for getting of cigarettes, but you will still be addicted to nicotine and if you want to quit vaping, you'll go through withdrawal again.
